title: Readability.MaxFunctionLength AST check
description:
Hardcoded limit (50 logical lines). Config arrives in cd-9.

Measure on:
- FunctionDeclaration
- FunctionExpression
- ArrowFunctionExpression (when body is BlockStatement)
- MethodDefinition

Skip arrow bodies that are expressions (`x => x + 1`) — those are by definition short.

Length = end line - start line of the body block. Don't count comments? Punt that to a config option later.

Acceptance:
- 51-line function: one finding
- 50-line function: no finding
- Nested function: each measured independently
- base_priority: -5 (Readability)

title: Cofferdam config file (cofferdam.toml)
description:
Deferred from phase 1 main scope but blocks much of phase 1's usefulness on real codebases. Schema for v0:

[checks."Readability.MaxLineLength"]
limit = 120
severity = "warning"
enabled = true

[checks."Readability.MaxFunctionLength"]
limit = 50

[checks."Design.MaxParameters"]
limit = 5

Discovery:
- Walk up from CWD until cofferdam.toml found, OR git root
- Empty/missing → all defaults
- Per-directory overrides? Defer to phase 3 with severity-axis work

Should land before cd-8 (smoke test) so we can tune the thresholds against real code.

title: Smoke-test cofferdam against a real TS repo
description:
After cd-1 and at least cd-4 ship, validate end-to-end against a real codebase. Pick something small but non-trivial.

Candidates:
- tinybench (one-file lib)
- @oxc-project/oxc-ast (small, TS-heavy)
- A vendored snapshot — never npm install, never network at test time

Plan:
- Clone target into examples/external/ (gitignored)
- Add a script: scripts/smoke.sh that runs cofferdam against it
- Capture the output as a golden file: tests/fixtures/smoke-tinybench.txt
- Goal: NO panics, NO parse failures on legal TS, sensible findings count, completion under 2s

Findings to investigate in the output:
- Are MaxFunctionLength findings reasonable? (Or is 50 too aggressive?)
- Does TripleEquals catch real `==` cases?
- Any unexpected Readability.MaxLineLength noise from prettier-formatted code?

title: Stopgap npm wrapper (postinstall binary download)
description:
Phase 4 (cd-napi epic) ships @cofferdam/node via napi-rs prebuilt binaries — that's weeks of work. Meanwhile we want TS users to type `pnpm add -D cofferdam` and have it work TODAY.

Approach: thin npm package whose postinstall hook downloads the matching GitHub Release binary. Pattern used by esbuild (early), wasm-pack, biome (early days), etc.

Steps:
1. Create packages/cofferdam/ with a minimal package.json + scripts/postinstall.js
2. postinstall detects platform/arch (process.platform + process.arch), maps to a release artifact URL, downloads + extracts to node_modules/.bin/cofferdam
3. Bin entry in package.json so `pnpm exec cofferdam` resolves
4. CI: publish to npm on tag push (alongside the existing release.yml)
5. Document in README: `pnpm add -D cofferdam` then `pnpm exec cofferdam check src/`

Phase 4 will replace this with the napi-rs path transparently — same package name, users don't notice. The postinstall approach has known issues (corporate proxies, offline CI, sandboxed npm installs) that the napi-rs prebuilt approach solves; until phase 4 lands, this is the bridge.

Acceptance:
- Tom can `pnpm add -D cofferdam` in rovikore-landing-page and run `pnpm exec cofferdam check src/` without any other setup
- Works on macOS, Linux, Windows (x64 minimum; arm64 if release matrix produces it)
- postinstall failure has a clear error message pointing to the manual install path

title: Plugin API surface
description:
Track A from the API design session: the public contract for plugin authors, modeled on Credo's check API but lifted to TS via napi-rs. Three pattern families need first-class support, derived from real custom checks in rovikore-host:

A. Line walk + magic-comment exemptions (BrandCasing, NoHardcodedDomain)
B. AST prewalk pattern-match (NoFloatPrices, NoHttpClientExceptReq)
C. Stateful walk with file-level decision (TenantIsolation, ApiFirst)

The 8 sub-issues below cover the design + implementation chunks. ★ marks must-haves before any plugin is useful.

Out of scope (separate epics later): Tier 0 declarative checks (cofferdam.toml match patterns), Rust-native cdylib plugins.

title: [A1★] LineView API + line classification
description:
Expose `file.lines()` returning `{ lineNo, text, isComment, isDocComment, isStringLiteral, isPragma }`. Required by Pattern A checks (BrandCasing, NoHardcodedDomain).

The classification flags need to come from the AST + token map so they're accurate (a regex check for `^\s*//` misses block comments split across lines). Internally, line classification piggybacks on oxc's comment/token data.

Acceptance:
- `file.lines()` returns iterable with all flags populated
- Block comments correctly classify all spanned lines
- Template literal lines are flagged (avoids false positives on user-facing strings inside backticks)

title: [A2★] AST surface for plugins
description:
Three access patterns from rovikore-host checks:
1. `file.ast.findAll(nodeType)` → eager filter by node kind (NoBannedHttpClient on ImportDeclaration / CallExpression)
2. `file.ast.walk(visitor)` → imperative visitor (TenantIsolation accumulating state)
3. Direct rooted access (`file.ast.root`) for surgical inspection

Requires deciding the TS-side AST shape — likely a thin TS proxy over oxc's serialized AST rather than re-parsing in TS.

Acceptance:
- Three rovikore checks (BrandCasing, NoHttpClient, TenantIsolation) implementable with no SDK gaps
- Span data on every node maps back to byte offsets (autofix can splice)
- Visitor short-circuit support (`return false` to stop descent)

title: [A3★] Per-check options schema
[A4] Suppression directives (// cofferdam-disable-...)
description:
Engine-level suppression so individual checks don't reinvent the wheel (rovikore-host's BrandCasing has its own `# brand:ignore` parser — that should become unnecessary).

Directives:
- `// cofferdam-disable-next-line ID1, ID2` — suppress next line
- `// cofferdam-disable-line ID1` — suppress current line (trailing comment)
- `// cofferdam-disable-file` — at top of file
- `// cofferdam-disable-block` ... `// cofferdam-enable-block` — between markers
- ID-less form suppresses all (with warning)

Engine-side: filter Issues post-collection by line + check_id against directives parsed from the file's comment map.

Migration plan: rovikore-host `# brand:ignore — <why>` becomes `// cofferdam-disable-next-line Rovikore.BrandCasing — <why>`.

title: [A5] Declarative file scoping
description:
Each check declares `files: { extensions, pathPattern, excludePatterns }` so engine skips inapplicable files cheaply (no parse, no run() call).

Replaces the `scannable?/1` boilerplate every rovikore check writes today.

```ts
files: {
  extensions: ["ts", "tsx"],
  pathPattern: "**/resources/**",
  excludePatterns: ["**/dev_checks/**"],
}
```

Engine evaluates these against discovery output before invoking run(). Per-check exclusions also overridable in cofferdam.toml.

title: [A6] ctx.report with fix payload
description:
`ctx.report({ message, span | line+column, fix? })` — the fix is an optional list of text edits that autofix consumes in phase 3.

```ts
ctx.report({
  message: "...",
  span: node.span,
  fix: ctx.replaceText(node.source.span, '"@org/http"'),
});
```

Helpers: `ctx.replaceText(span, str)`, `ctx.insertBefore(span, str)`, `ctx.insertAfter(span, str)`, `ctx.removeRange(span)`.

Out of scope here: the autofix interactive engine. This issue just lands the data shape on Issue + ctx helpers.

Acceptance:
- Issue includes optional `fix: TextEdit[]` after serialization
- Round-trips through napi without loss

title: [A7] TS plugin loader (napi worker_threads)
description:
Phase 4 deliverable. Each plugin module loads into its own worker_thread for crash containment + per-plugin timeout. Engine sends `Run` messages with serialized SourceFile + AST handle, gets back Issue[] over the wire.

Depends on the broader napi-rs FFI surface (already cd-napi epic territory in the existing plan).

Acceptance:
- A plugin file under .cofferdam/checks/ is auto-loaded
- Plugin throwing during run() is contained — that file emits a Warning.PluginCrashed and analysis continues
- Plugin run timeout enforced (default 5s; configurable)

title: [A8] @cofferdam/check-sdk npm package
description:
The package plugin authors install. Exports:
- `defineCheck` — typed factory that returns the Check object napi expects
- `Category`, `Severity` — enums matching Rust types
- AST node type definitions (likely generated from oxc-ast)
- Helper utils: `isComment`, span builders, line iteration, fix helpers

Published with the same prebuilt binaries via napi-rs template (Linux/Mac/Windows — already in release.yml).

Acceptance:
- `pnpm add @cofferdam/check-sdk` and write a check in <30 lines (matching the BrandCasing example from API design session)
- TypeScript types are tight enough that an invalid AST property access fails to compile
- README has at least one example per pattern (line-walk, AST findAll, stateful walk)

title: Robot mode — compact line-delim format
description:
JSON output (cd-yvm) is functional but 1.85x text mode bytes due to repeated field names per finding (366 findings × full schema = bloat). For real token economy, ship a one-finding-per-line pipe-delimited format alongside JSON.

Proposed: `--format=compact` emits a single header line + one record per finding:

```
priority|severity|category|id|file|line|column|message
-5|warning|readability|Readability.MaxLineLength|examples/sample.ts|8|121|line is 149 characters, exceeds limit of 120
```

- Stable header — parsers split on pipe
- Messages with literal pipes get backslash-escaped
- Well-formed even when zero findings (header only)

Inspired by cass's `--robot-format compact` pattern. JSON stays the canonical machine format; compact is the agent-shoveling-context-into-prompt format.

Acceptance:
- 200-finding run produces output ≤ 35% of text formatter's bytes (and ≤ 50% of JSON)
- Header documented at `docs/output-formats.md`
- `--robot --format=compact` is a valid combo

title: [Docs] Plugin SDK author guide
description:
Narrative companion to cd-81a.8 (the @cofferdam/check-sdk package). Walks an author from 'I want to enforce this rule in my repo' to 'shipped plugin'.

Sections:
- Three pattern families (line walk, AST visitor, stateful walk) with one example each
- Mapping from popular ESLint custom rules to cofferdam plugins
- Migrating Credo custom checks to cofferdam (using the rovikore-host examples as case studies)
- Testing your plugin (the SDK ships a test harness)
- Publishing under @yourorg/cofferdam-checks-*

title: Design.MaxParameters AST check
description:
Hardcoded limit (5 params). Cheap counter check — validates that base_priority on Check::meta is ergonomic for tunable thresholds.

Counts on FormalParameters node. Counts:
- Regular params
- Default-valued params (`x = 1`)
- Rest params (`...args` counts as 1)
- Destructured params (`{ a, b }` counts as 1, not 2)

Acceptance:
- 6-param function: one finding
- 5-param function: no finding
- Destructured: `function f({ a, b, c, d, e, f, g })` — one param, no finding
- base_priority: 5 (Design)

title: Wire oxc as the TypeScript parser
description:
Add oxc_parser + oxc_ast as workspace deps in cofferdam-core. Parse SourceFile lazily on first AST access. Decide span shape (oxc::span::Span vs our current Span — likely keep both, with conversion).

Open questions to resolve in the PR:
- Where does the AST live? Owned by SourceFile? CheckContext?
- How do we handle TSX vs TS (parser flag)?
- Error handling: how do we report parse failures? (Probably: emit a Warning.ParseError issue and skip other checks for that file.)

Acceptance:
- oxc parses examples/sample.ts without error
- A new field on CheckContext exposes the AST to checks
- MaxLineLength still works (proves we didn't break the text-only path)
- A parse-error fixture file produces exactly one Warning.ParseError issue, no panics

title: User-facing documentation
description:
No user-facing docs beyond README today. Need a coherent docs/ tree before announcing v0.x to anyone.

Sub-issues capture the discrete pages. Layout target: `docs/` at repo root, indexed from README, eventually published via mdBook or similar.

Out of scope: API docs (rustdoc handles those), architecture decision records (separate ADR track), changelogs (auto-generated from release notes).

title: Add unit + integration tests for cofferdam-core and engine
description:
Phase 0 has zero tests. Lock in the contract before AST work expands the surface.

Unit tests (cofferdam-core):
- Priority ordering: HIGHER > NORMAL > LOW > LOWER
- Severity::default() == Warning
- Span byte/line/column construction is consistent
- Category::ALL covers all five variants

Integration test (cofferdam-engine):
- Engine::analyze on examples/sample.ts produces exactly one Issue
- Issue.check_id == "Readability.MaxLineLength"
- Issue is in the Readability bucket after sort

Set up a test/ directory pattern and add to ci.yml's cargo test step (already runs).

title: [Docs] Output formats (text, json, future)
description:
Reference for every --format value. Schema for json (lands with cd-yvm), header for compact (lands with cd-ab2), eventual SARIF + GitHub Annotations.

Each format documented with:
- When to use it
- Example output
- Schema or field-by-field description
- Stability guarantee (which fields are part of the contract)

title: [Docs] Built-in check catalog
description:
One page per built-in check (or one big indexed page if the catalog stays under ~30). Each entry:
- ID (Category.Name)
- Default priority + severity
- What it flags + why
- Code example (bad → good)
- Configuration options
- Suppression directive examples

Pages auto-generated from CheckMeta + a hand-written body file is the long-term play. v1: hand-written, regenerate when adding a check.

Acceptance: every check in all_builtins() has an entry. Stub Consistency.QuoteStyle and Refactor.CognitiveComplexity are marked 'planned'.

title: [Docs] CI integration recipes
description:
Copy-paste workflows for the major CI systems:
- GitHub Actions (with --robot output → step summary, --since main → PR-only mode, SARIF → Code Scanning once cd-snv-era SARIF lands)
- GitLab CI
- CircleCI
- Drone / generic

For each: minimal yaml, recommendation on caching, severity-gating pattern, baseline-file pattern.

title: Default-skip .d.ts files in discovery
description:
Generated declaration files (`*.d.ts`) dominate findings on real repos — e.g. Cloudflare `worker-configuration.d.ts` produces hundreds of MaxLineLength hits that no human will fix.

Decision: default-skip `.d.ts` for syntactic checks. Re-include via:
- `--include-declarations` CLI flag
- Per-check opt-in (some type-aware checks in phase 5 will need them)

Implementation:
- Add `include_declarations: bool` to DiscoveryOptions (default false)
- When false, drop files ending in `.d.ts` / `.d.mts` / `.d.cts`
- CLI flag wires through

Validates against: rovikore-landing-page goes from ~50 findings to a handful.

Acceptance:
- Default run on rovikore-landing-page produces fewer than 5 findings (down from 50+)
- `cofferdam check --include-declarations` reproduces the noisy output
- Test fixture covers .d.ts, .d.mts, .d.cts

title: Normalize path separators in output
description:
On Windows, output mixes forward and backslashes (e.g. `C:/Users/tajdi/rovikore-landing-page\worker-configuration.d.ts`) because the user-supplied root uses one and the walker emits the other.

Fix: normalize all displayed paths to forward slashes (cross-platform consistency, matches what most editors/CI tools expect for source links).

Acceptance:
- Output paths use `/` only
- File paths still resolve correctly when clicked in editors
- Span byte offsets unaffected

title: Warning.TripleEquals AST check
description:
Flag uses of `==` and `!=` (vs `===`/`!==`). Walks oxc BinaryExpression nodes.

Edge cases to handle:
- typeof comparisons against "undefined"/"null" (still flag — config can suppress later)
- `x == null` is the one common idiom that's intentionally loose; keep flagging it for now and revisit when we add per-rule config (cd-9)

Acceptance:
- Fixture file with `==` produces a Warning.TripleEquals finding with span pointing to the operator
- `===` produces no finding
- base_priority: 15 (Warning category default)
- Severity::Error default for Warning category checks once severity-axis lands (note for phase 3)

title: Switch zig setup action to mlugg/setup-zig
description:
release.yml uses korandoru/setup-zig@v1. mlugg/setup-zig is the more actively maintained alternative — most modern Rust+Zig CI pipelines have moved to it. Same API, different repo.

Switch happens in .github/workflows/release.yml. Verify with workflow_dispatch on the build job before tagging next release.

title: Walk directories + glob in cofferdam check
description:
Replace the phase-0 ad-hoc list of file paths with directory walk + glob support in `cofferdam check`. Default include pattern: `**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts}`. Respect `.gitignore` and `.cofferdamignore` via the `ignore` crate. Single-threaded walk is fine; rayon parallelism comes when oxc lands (cd-3).

Acceptance:
- `cofferdam check` (no args) walks CWD
- `cofferdam check src/` walks the directory
- Files matching .gitignore are skipped
- Output unchanged shape (still grouped by category, priority-sorted)
- Test: walks examples/ and finds the long line in sample.ts

title: Distribute cofferdam binary releases (pre-npm)
description:
Cut binary releases NOW so the user can pin cofferdam in their own repos before phase 4's full napi-rs npm publish lands. Enables real-world iteration via dogfooding.

Distribution paths:
1. **GitHub Releases**: tag-triggered, multi-platform binaries from the existing release.yml matrix (Linux x64/arm64 gnu+musl, macOS x64/arm64, Windows x64/arm64). Users `curl | tar` or download. — closest to today's tooling.
2. **cargo install**: `cargo install --git https://github.com/cofferdam/cofferdam cofferdam-cli` — Rust users, works today without any release infra.
3. **homebrew-cofferdam tap**: `brew install cofferdam/tap/cofferdam` — macOS dev experience.
4. **Scoop bucket** (Windows): user already uses scoop heavily.

Phase 4 will replace #1-#3 with the full `@cofferdam/node` npm distribution (the platform-specific binaries via napi-rs prebuilt artifacts). Until then:

Acceptance:
- `v0.0.2` tagged + GH Release published with at minimum linux-x64, mac-arm64, windows-x64 binaries
- Release workflow flips from `if: false` to gated on tag pushes (matches napi-rs template's pattern)
- Install-once instructions in README for each platform
- User can run `cofferdam check` in rovikore-landing-page and one other repo without local clone

Out of scope: npm publish, crates.io publish, Linux distros. Phase 4 / phase 6 territory.

title: Test corpus — vendored real-world TS repos
description:
Curate a corpus of real-world TS repos as test fixtures. Goal: catch regressions and parse-corner-cases on real code, not just hand-crafted samples.

Approach: vendor as git submodules at known commits (or snapshot tarballs) under `tests/corpus/` (gitignored, populated by `scripts/fetch-corpus.sh`).

Initial corpus picks (small + diverse parser stress):
- tinybench (one-file lib, modern TS)
- zod (heavy use of generics, conditional types)
- @oxc-project/oxc-ast (oxc's own TS bindings — meta)
- Cloudflare worker-types (the .d.ts noise source we already saw)
- One Vite/React app (e.g. rovikore-landing-page if user OKs vendoring) for JSX coverage

Test patterns:
- snapshot test: golden output per repo, regenerated via `UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 cargo test corpus`
- perf assertion: each corpus repo's analysis must complete in N ms
- zero-panic: any panic during corpus scan fails the test

Distinct from cd-61j (one-off smoke test). This is the durable test infrastructure.

title: Refactor.UnusedVariable AST check
description:
Local-binding scope only — no cross-file analysis (that's phase 5 / type-aware).

Edge cases:
- Destructuring: `const { a, b } = obj` — flag each unused binding individually
- Rest patterns: `const [a, ...rest] = arr` — rest is always considered used (intentional)
- Underscore prefix: `_unused` is conventionally suppressed — don't flag
- Function parameters: flag unused params (with same _-prefix exception)
- Catch parameters: `catch (e)` where e is unused — flag

Out of scope (defer to cd-9 / phase 5):
- Imports (handled by tree-shaker, not here)
- Class fields (need type info to be precise)

Acceptance:
- Fixture covering each edge case above
- base_priority: 10 (Refactor)

title: Robot mode — AI-first JSON output
description:
Token-economical structured output for AI agents (Claude Code, Cursor, aider, etc.).

Flags:
- `--robot` / `--json` — machine-readable output, stable schema, no ANSI, no banner, no totals line
- `--robot --format=toon` — token-optimized format (1.6x more efficient than JSON for repeated keys)
- `--robot-meta` — include cursor + token-budget metadata for paginated runs

Schema (initial draft):
```json
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "id": "Warning.TripleEquals",
      "category": "warning",
      "priority": 15,
      "severity": "warning",
      "file": "src/foo.ts",
      "line": 42,
      "column": 8,
      "endLine": 42,
      "endColumn": 10,
      "message": "Use === instead of ==",
      "fix": null
    }
  ],
  "summary": { "total": 1, "byCategory": { "warning": 1 }, "durationMs": 183 }
}
```

Why P1: most cofferdam usage will be agent-driven from day one. The text formatter exists for humans; robot mode is the load-bearing surface. Should land before any check work is announced externally.

Acceptance:
- `cofferdam check src/ --robot` produces parseable JSON, exit code matches text mode
- Schema documented + JSON Schema artifact at `schemas/findings.schema.json` for tooling
- Token cost on a 200-finding run ≤ 30% of the text formatter's

title: [Docs] Suppression directives reference
description:
Reference for the engine-level suppression syntax (lands with cd-81a.4). Forms:
- // cofferdam-disable-next-line ID1, ID2 [— reason]
- // cofferdam-disable-line ID1
- // cofferdam-disable-file
- // cofferdam-disable-block ... // cofferdam-enable-block
- ID-less form (suppresses all, with engine warning)

Notes on:
- 'reason required?' option (default off, on for Warning category)
- Why we chose // cofferdam-disable-* over the shorter forms (avoid clashes with eslint-disable)
- How suppression interacts with baselines
